cases.title: fix: handle destroyed image capture sources gracefully

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## Summary

When a capture source (output, workspace, or toplevel) is destroyed before a session interacts with it, the `Destroyed` variant is reached in `ImageCopyCaptureHandler` methods. Previously this triggered `unreachable!()`, crashing the compositor.

This patch handles the `Destroyed` case gracefully:
- `new_session` / `new_cursor_session`: return without setup
- `session_destroyed` / `cursor_session_destroyed`: return without cleanup  
- `frame`: explicitly fail the frame with `CaptureFailureReason::Unknown` to notify the client rather than silently dropping

## Architectural note

The `Output` variant already handles lifecycle races cleanly via `WeakOutput` — when the output is gone, `weak.upgrade()` returns `None` and the handler returns gracefully. The `Workspace` and `Toplevel` variants use strong references, which is why the `Destroyed` fallback variant exists.

A deeper fix would be to use weak references for `Workspace` and `Toplevel` as well, making the `Destroyed` variant unnecessary. This has broader implications across the codebase, so it is left as a recommendation for maintainers to evaluate.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reproduce by destroying a capture source while a session is active
- [ ] Verify compositor no longer crashes on `unreachable!()`
- [ ] Verify client receives frame failure notification

cases.title: Respect cursor_follows_focus when activating a window on another output

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## Problem

When clicking an app in the dock/panel while its window is on a **different output**, the pointer is warped to the center of that window — even when **Cursor follows focus** is disabled in Settings. This is surprising and disruptive on multi-monitor setups (you click on monitor A, the window focuses on monitor B, and your cursor is yanked to B).

This is the root cause behind several reports:
- #930 (moving focus between monitors centers the cursor)
- pop-os/cosmic-settings#1269
- pop-os/cosmic-epoch#3121

## Cause

In `src/wayland/handlers/toplevel_management.rs`, the `activate` handler warps the pointer whenever `switching_output` is true, without checking the `cursor_follows_focus` config. Every other focus path in the compositor (`shell::focus::update_focus_state` at `focus/mod.rs`, and `input::actions`) already gates the warp on `cursor_follows_focus`; this path was missed.

## Fix

Gate the pointer warp on `self.common.config.cosmic_conf.cursor_follows_focus`. Keyboard focus and `set_active_output` are unchanged — only the pointer warp becomes conditional, consistent with the rest of the codebase.

When `cursor_follows_focus` is **enabled**, behavior is unchanged (cursor still follows to the window on the other output). When **disabled**, the cursor stays where it is.

## Testing

- Two monitors, `cursor_follows_focus` disabled: click an app in the dock whose window is on the other monitor → cursor no longer jumps. ✅
- `cursor_follows_focus` enabled: cursor still follows to the activated window. ✅

cases.title: dbus: expose active Wayland idle-inhibitors over the session bus

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## Problem

Only the compositor knows which clients hold a Wayland idle-inhibitor
(`zwp_idle_inhibitor_v1`). Nothing else can enumerate them, so a tray/applet
cannot tell the user which application is currently preventing the session from
going idle / suspending — most commonly a browser playing video.

## Change

Expose the active idle-inhibitors over a small session-bus interface:

- Name `com.system76.CosmicComp`, path `/com/system76/CosmicComp`
- Interface `com.system76.CosmicComp.IdleInhibit`
- Method `ListInhibitors() -> a(us)` — `(pid, app_id)` per inhibiting surface

## Implementation

- A shared `Arc<Mutex<HashMap<surface_id, (pid, app_id)>>>` is updated in the
  `IdleInhibitHandler::inhibit`/`uninhibit` handlers (client pid resolved from
  the surface at inhibit time).
- A dedicated thread runs a blocking zbus server reading that map. It is fully
  decoupled from the calloop loop and every failure only logs, so it can never
  affect the compositor.
- No new dependencies (zbus is already used).

## Motivation

Enables a "what's keeping the system awake" applet
(https://github.com/lxp-git/cosmic-ext-applet-inhibit-status), which merges this
with logind inhibitors and a companion cosmic-idle change that exposes
`org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` inhibitors. Related: pop-os/cosmic-idle#4.

## Testing

Built and run on 1.2.0: the applet lists e.g. Chrome's Wayland idle-inhibitor
with its pid while a video plays, and the entry clears when released. Cherry-picks
cleanly onto `master` (the touched handlers are unchanged).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

cases.title: feat: add Grid workspace layout

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
Implements the compositor half of pop-os/cosmic-workspaces-epoch#51 (grid-arranged workspaces).

- New `WorkspaceLayout::Grid` variant plus `workspace_grid_columns` / `workspace_grid_rows` (serde defaults 3/2, backward compatible) in `cosmic-comp-config`
- Grid mode keeps a fixed `columns x rows` workspace count (padded up, never destroying occupied workspaces) instead of the dynamic trailing-empty behavior; supported in both `OutputBound` and `Global` modes
- `Next/Previous/MoveTo/SendToWorkspace` become direction-aware in Grid mode via the binding's inferred direction: Left/Right move within the row, Up/Down move by a full row, both wrapping row/column-locally (respecting `workspace_wraparound`); `Focus`/`Move` at grid edges stay in the grid instead of falling through to `SwitchOutput`/`MoveToOutput`
- 4-finger swipes navigate in all four directions (`SwipeAction::GridMove`), honoring natural scrolling; swipe-end velocity normalizes against the axis of the move
- The switch animation slides along the axis of the actual move
- Workspace protocol coordinates are published as 2D `[column, row]` while Grid is active, so clients (e.g. the workspaces overview) can lay out the real grid; linear coordinates are restored when leaving Grid
- Grid math is unit-tested (`grid_tests`, 9 cases incl. wraparound + degenerate dimensions)

Vertical/Horizontal behavior is unchanged; existing config files parse unmodified.

Companion PRs: pop-os/cosmic-settings#2073 (Grid option UI) and pop-os/cosmic-workspaces-epoch#318 (grid overview).

cases.title: feat: per-application workspace assignment rules

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
Implements pop-os/cosmic-epoch#1395 / pop-os/cosmic-workspaces-epoch#186: opening an app always places it on a chosen workspace.

Adds a `workspace_assignments` config to `com.system76.CosmicComp` — a list of `(app_id, workspace)` rules (workspace numbers 1-based, matching the UI). When a new window's `app_id` matches, it maps to that workspace instead of the active one, regardless of launch origin; the target workspace is flagged urgent rather than stealing focus (same behavior as other windows mapped to inactive workspaces). Rules hot-reload like other compositor settings.

Rules can be managed from the **window context menu**: right-click a titlebar → *Always open on this workspace* toggles a rule for that app on the window's current workspace (the entry then shows *Always opens on workspace N* with a checkmark). The menu writes through cosmic-config, so the config file stays the single source of truth:

```ron
// ~/.config/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicComp/v1/workspace_assignments
[
    (app_id: "code", workspace: 5),
]
```

**Alt+Space opens the window menu.** Not every window has a compositor-drawn titlebar to right-click — client-side-decorated windows (most GTK4/Qt6/Electron/libcosmic apps, including COSMIC's own Files) have none, so there was previously no way to reach the context menu (and therefore the workspace-assignment toggle) for them at all. Alt+Space is added as a hardcoded, non-configurable compositor shortcut (`PrivateAction::OpenWindowMenu`) that opens the menu for the currently focused window regardless of decoration mode — chosen because it's unused by default and is the traditional "window system menu" shortcut on other desktops (Super+M was the first attempt, but that's already bound to Maximize by default, so it's Alt+Space instead).

**Rename support.** The `zcosmic_workspace_handle_v2::rename` request was defined in the protocol but never handled compositor-side; this wires it up (advertises the `Rename` capability, applies the name, and persists it for pinned workspaces) so clients can let users rename workspaces.

Happy to follow up with a cosmic-settings page for bulk management if the config shape is acceptable.

cases.title: Implement wp_tearing_control_v1 (composited tearing)

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## What

Implements `wp_tearing_control_v1` with **composited tearing** — async page flips of the compositor's own composited buffer. Addresses #248.

- Protocol: `wp_tearing_control_manager_v1` (v1) global; per-surface double-buffered presentation hint (promoted on commit, `tearing_control_exists` error on duplicate controls, destroy resets pending to vsync).
- Policy: an output enters tearing mode iff an opt-in toggle is set (`COSMIC_ALLOW_TEARING=1` env for now), the output is not mirroring, and the focused fullscreen toplevel's committed hint is `async`.
- Frame clock: in tearing mode the estimated-vblank throttle is bypassed — composite is driven by client commits (rate-ceiled ~500fps) and submitted with `FrameFlags::ALLOW_ASYNC_PAGE_FLIP`; frame callbacks are sent immediately, so clients run uncapped.
- Cursor plane is disabled in tearing mode (cursor composites instead): kernel atomic async flips may only change the primary plane FB, so this keeps every async commit valid.
- Depends on smithay async-flip support: Smithay/smithay#2099 (Cargo patch currently points at that branch).

## Why composited tearing

On muxless hybrid laptops (game renders on the dGPU, iGPU scans out the internal panel) direct scanout of client buffers is impossible — the classic "tearing only for direct-scanout fullscreen" design delivers nothing on such machines. Async-flipping the composited buffer does: validated end-to-end on an i915-scanout + NVIDIA-render laptop, CS2 (native Wayland, fullscreen) runs 240fps on a 144Hz eDP with visible tearing, where it was previously FIFO-capped at 144. Compositor cost went *down* (composite-per-commit at ~240/s measured cheaper than the previous 144Hz vsync path in CPU time). Zero rejected async flips observed on i915.

## Current limitations (draft status — seeking direction)

- Composited-tearing only; the direct-scanout fullscreen path does not async-flip yet (planned follow-up — needed for single-GPU desktops).
- Single-output policy; no VRR interaction handling yet.
- Toggle is an env var; should become cosmic-config + Settings UI.
- Xwayland (24.1.12) did not forward tearing hints for an X11 Vulkan IMMEDIATE client on the NVIDIA stack during testing — under investigation whether that's driver- or Xwayland-side; native Wayland clients work.
- No `DRM_CAP_ATOMIC_ASYNC_PAGE_FLIP` gating yet (tracked in the smithay PR).

Implementation was developed with AI assistance and human review/testing on real hardware; happy to iterate per maintainer direction and split/reshape as preferred.

## Advertise `xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1`

This adds `xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1` support to `cosmic-comp`.

### Why?

Applications using `winit` currently produce the following warning when running under `cosmic-comp`:

```text
xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1 is not supported
```

The protocol was already handled correctly by the client and applications continued to function normally. The missing compositor global only caused `winit` to emit a warning.

This change advertises the protocol through Smithay, allowing clients to detect its availability and eliminating the warning.

### Changes

* Add an `xdg_toplevel_icon` Wayland handler.
* Implement `XdgToplevelIconHandler` for `State`.
* Create and advertise `XdgToplevelIconManager`.
* Keep the manager alive as part of `Common`.

Smithay handles the protocol requests and maintains the cached toplevel icon state. This change does not alter COSMIC's existing window behavior or add icon integration to the compositor UI.

### Testing

* `cargo check` passes successfully.
* Tested with the Smithay revision currently used by `cosmic-comp`.

### Impact

No existing functionality was broken before this change. The primary purpose of this change is to advertise the already-supported Wayland protocol and remove the unnecessary client-side warning.

cases.title: fix: back off and give up on repeated render submit failures

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
Closes #2688

## Problem

When the kernel rejects every atomic commit for an output, the redraw timer in `queue_redraw` re-queues a
forced redraw immediately after each failure, with no delay and no limit. smithay logs
`New screen configuration invalid!` with the full `AtomicRequest` dump on every attempt, so the loop
floods the journal (in #2688 it filled 158 GiB of disk in 18.5 h) and keeps the compositor busy.

The dead output's `DrmCompositor` also stays registered with the `DrmOutputManager`. `use_mode`,
`initialize_output` and `allow_primary_scanout_any` submit on every registered compositor, so
output-configuration requests for the *other* outputs fail as well, and the first
`cosmic-randr disable` of the dead output is rejected (`Failed to switch primary-plane scanout flags`).

## Change

In the surface thread (`src/backend/kms/surface/mod.rs`, first commit) and the DPMS handler
(`src/wayland/handlers/output_power.rs`, second commit):

- A redraw that fails before KMS takes the frame retries after an exponential back-off: one frame
  time, doubling, capped at 4 s. Redraw requests during the back-off wait for it.
- After 12 consecutive failures, if the error chain contains a `DrmError` (KMS rejected the frame),
  the surface stops rendering and deactivates the same way a session pause does (`active = false`,
  `DrmOutput` dropped). The next `apply_config_for_outputs` then disables or re-initializes it; that
  also happens on VT switch / session resume and on a DRM udev change.
- Other errors (e.g. no renderer after a GPU reset) keep retrying at the cap and never give up, since
  they clear by themselves.
- The failure count resets on the first frame KMS accepts, on resume, and on DPMS off.
- When outputs are powered on (input or wlr-output-power) and a woken surface has given up, the
  output config is re-applied once on idle (`refresh_output_config()`, as on a DRM udev change), so a
  later wake can still bring the output back. The old loop recovered that way: on the rig below, 2 of
  6 stuck episodes on the stock build healed by themselves at a later wake (2 of 8 wakes while stuck).
- Logging is per state change: first failure (warn), giving up (error), recovery and
  re-initialization (warn, so the episode is closed at the default log level).

Out of scope: why the commit is rejected in the first place, and smithay logging the whole atomic
request at warn level. Known limitation, shared with session resume and hotplug:
`apply_config_for_outputs` stops at the first output that fails to initialize, so if two outputs gave
up and one still fails at wake, the other is not re-initialized either. And while a given-up output
stays enabled in the config, a request that keeps it enabled (e.g. any change from the display
settings) retries it and is rejected if the kernel still refuses; disabling it is accepted. Marking
such an output disabled in the config would avoid that, but is a policy change left for a follow-up.

## Testing

Fedora 44, NVIDIA GTX 1060 on 580.178.04, three outputs (DP-1 3840x2160@120, DP-3 and HDMI-A-1
2560x1440@100). One output intermittently fails to come back after the screens sleep (HDMI-A-1
on 6 of 18 wakes from a healthy state between 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-02 on the stock build; DP-3 in
the patched run below), with the same `Atomic Test failed for new properties on crtc` /
`Error setting crtc ... Invalid argument` errors as #2688.

| | stock 1.8.0 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| render failures after the wake | 1,300-3,500/s (logged + journald-suppressed), unbounded | 11 attempts in 14 s, then gives up |
| cosmic-comp log lines of its own | one per attempt | 2 (first failure, giving up) |
| cosmic-comp CPU | ~110% | ~13% (idle) |
| `cosmic-randr list` / kernel for the dead output | enabled / disabled | enabled / disabled until reconfigured |
| `cosmic-randr disable <dead output>` | 1st rejected, 2nd accepted | 1st accepted |
| re-enabling it afterwards (mode change script) | works after the 2nd disable | works, no log-out |

The re-apply on wake, on device, twice: after a system suspend/resume the session-resume reload could
not re-initialize DP-3 (`Invalid argument` from the kernel), which leaves the output dark on the stock
build too; and HDMI-A-1 gave up 14 s after a natural wake. In both cases the next DPMS off/on
re-applied the config and the output came back with no manual steps.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (default and `debug` features),
`cargo check --no-default-features` and `cargo test` pass; `--all-features` (tracy) was not built
locally. Unit tests cover the back-off sequence and the KMS-rejection classification.

cases.title: backend: dmabuf: ensure primary render node is preffered

label.rationale: Merged, no filled disclosure, no slop language, no hard markers.

cases.body:
After dmabuf-v6 support in #2513, `update_default_feedback()` adds every non-primary GPU using `add_preference_tranche()`. Smithay intentionally places those tranches before the implicit main tranche.
As a result, the current default feedback ordering is
```
secondary 1
secondary 2
primary
```

and not the desired

```
primary
secondary 1
secondary 2
```
For v6 clients, secondary GPU becomes the first/default Sampling device even though `cosmic-comp` selected another GPU as `primary_node`.
On my AMD iGPU + RTX 4060 laptop, before this fix `cosmic-panel`, `cosmic-workspaces` and EGL clients selected NVIDIA by default. 

After the fix, applications now select the integrated GPU again, matching the behavior before the dmabuf-v6 update.

cases.title: Optional approval mode: keep a build-time-trusted window above everything and ignore libei input while it is up

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## What it does
This mode is off unless the build sets both `COSMIC_COMP_APPROVER_EXE` and `COSMIC_COMP_APPROVER_APP_ID`. Builds that set neither behave exactly as before.

When both are set, a Wayland toplevel is an approval window if two things hold:
- its client's executable (from the socket credentials, `/proc/<pid>/exe`) equals `COSMIC_COMP_APPROVER_EXE`;
- its app id equals `COSMIC_COMP_APPROVER_APP_ID`.

While an approval window is up:
- **Placement.** It is not placed on a workspace. A new render/input stage, right after the session lock, draws it centred on the active output, above overlay-layer surfaces.
- **Keyboard.** Only it can hold keyboard focus, so exclusive layer surfaces cannot take it.
- **Pointer.** Pointer input reaches it or nothing.
- **libei.** Input from `com.system76.CosmicComp.Ei` sender sockets is dropped. A new `test-input` Cargo feature lets that input through for test builds.

## Why
A desktop that asks the user to confirm a privileged action needs a confirmation window that no other client can cover, steal focus from, or click through with injected input. This follows the same reasoning as the session lock, but applies to a single trusted client.

## Files
- `src/shell/approval.rs` (new, with unit tests).
- Small hooks in `shell/mod.rs`, `shell/focus/{mod,order,target}.rs`, `input/mod.rs`, `backend/render/mod.rs`, `wayland/handlers/{compositor,xdg_shell/mod}.rs` and `libei.rs`.
- `Cargo.toml` gains `test-input = []`.

## Testing
- `cargo check` and `cargo test --lib approval` pass on master (41497b4), both with and without `test-input` and with the two variables set.
- A downstream VM suite for this patch on epoch-1.8.0 is written but has not run yet. On both builds it makes two attempts against an approval window: an overlay-layer surface that requests exclusive keyboard focus, and libei key events. I'll add its results here.

Opened as a draft to ask whether you would take this upstream, or would prefer another shape for it, such as a protocol or a config key instead of build-time variables.

cases.title: corner-radius: Clip subsurfaces with their own corner radius

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
Depends on pop-os/cosmic-protocols#93

Window and workspace thumbnails in the workspaces overview are subsurfaces, so the client cannot clip them and they always have square corners (pop-os/cosmic-workspaces-epoch#283).

This implements version 3 of `cosmic_corner_radius_manager_v1` (`get_corner_radius_subsurface`):

- The radius is stored in the same `CacheableCorners` cached state that toplevels use.
- When rendering the surface tree, a subsurface with its own radius is clipped to its bounds with the existing `ClippedSurfaceRenderElement`. No new shader is added. Subsurfaces without a radius render as before.
- Known limitation: a subsurface with its own radius is not also clipped by the rounded corners of its parent window.

Tested in a live COSMIC session together with the iced and cosmic-workspaces changes.

cases.title: fix: [ Input Method related ] only switch input source on the configu…

label.rationale: Closed without merge. Population sample, not a slop label.

cases.body:
## Bug

After switching to a non-US layout, almost any key flips the input source back to the default (e.g. `us`). The layout should only be changed by the configured `InputSourceSwitch` shortcut.

## Cause

Every key press could call `update_virtual_keyboard_keymap` without requiring the key + modifier to match the system config.

## Fix

- Only keys pressed with a modifier (Super/Ctrl/Alt/Shift) can ever update the   keymap or change the layout. Without a modifier, the handler returns early   and never touches the shortcut list.
- The layout can be changed only by the shortcut configured in system   settings: the pressed keycode and modifier must both match the configured   shortcut. 
- Unrelated keys no longer trigger a keymap update or a layout change.

## Tested

- Single modifier: `Super+Space`, `Ctrl+Space`, `Alt+Space`, `Shift+Space`  -   each switches only on its own shortcut.
- Combined modifiers: configurations like `Ctrl+Shift+Space` also work as  configured.
- Multiple different shortcut configs were tested and all behave correctly.
- Keys not configured as the shortcut never switch and never update the
  keymap, with or without modifiers.
